description: ASA Sports (ASAwins) review, checked 19 Nov 2026: package prices, the pay when you win wording, its own streak records and what bettors have said.
dek: A Wisconsin pick service run since 1997 by two former Doc's Sports handicappers. Packages run from $19.95 a day to $995 a season on its own site, and the same picks are sold on a network of affiliate sites. Its posted records are streaks from start dates it picks itself, and the only outside log we found, of its free picks, was 3-6 in the last 30 days.

short_answer: ASA is a real and long running business. Its own pages say Lee Kostroski and Mike Merlet started at Doc's Enterprises in the late 1980s and early 1990s and founded ASA Inc in 1997. The website terms name American Sports Analysts, Inc with a post office box in Verona, Wisconsin, and U.S. Treasury loan data lists American Sports Analysts Inc in Madison, Wisconsin, with a $9,600 PPP loan approved on 9 Apr 2020. The picks are sold on ASAwins.com, on a network of SportsCapping affiliate sites such as Vegas Experts, Boyd's Bets and Capper Reviews, and on Big Al's site.

The record is harder to judge. Every number we found is a streak from a start date ASA or its store chose: 50-33 in top college football plays since 29 Nov 2025, 92-73 in top football plays since 4 Dec 2025, 148-126 in top NBA plays since 30 Oct 2025. We checked the math and the win rates match, but the profits are modest: the NBA run is about +8.8 units over 274 plays. The same store's own text says the 3 day pass was 8-11 this season. A third party site that logs ASA's free picks had them at 3-6 and minus $362 over the last 30 days.

Forum talk about ASA is old and thin. In 2005 and 2006 TheRX members called the owners honest and easy to reach, while others mocked people who pay for picks. We found no recent buyer reviews anywhere we could open.

guarantee: On its own site ASA advertises a "pay only when you win" promise. The homepage says: "Every single-game and daily pick is backed by our “pay only when you win” guarantee or full guaranteed results." The free picks page repeats it as "PAY ONLY WHEN YOU WIN". We found no page that explains how it works, what counts as a win, or whether it covers the season packages. The site terms say only that materials are provided "as is" and that ASA "makes no warranties", and they do not mention refunds.

On the SportsCapping network the rules are written out. The guarantee policy says: "if you don’t show a profit during your paid subscription period, you’ll receive an equal-length subscription free of charge." It adds "We do not offer monetary refunds", grades every play at a flat 100 units whatever its star rating, gives only one free term per purchase, and states "There is no profit guarantee on season-long subscriptions." The refund policy says products are sold "as is" and "no refunds will be issued".
Neither version pays back what you lose on the bets themselves.

claims_note: The streaks each begin on a different date: 29 Nov 2025 for college football, 4 Dec 2025 for football, 30 Oct 2025 for the NBA, 9 Jun 2026 for hockey. A record that starts wherever it looks best is a common way to show a hot run. Ask for the full log from a fixed date.

The history claims do not agree with each other. ASAwins.com pages say "Handicapping since 1987", "Professional sports handicappers since 1989", "40+ years of experience" and "55+ years" combined, while the network bio says 50+ years combined and the NFL pass text still says the coming football season will be "our 23rd year in business", which would point to about 2003 or 2004 rather than 1997.
record: What is independently logged: only ASA's free picks. GameAdvisers, which says it found the picks on BestBettor.com, listed 10 ASA free picks from 24 Oct to 18 Nov 2026: 3 wins, 6 losses and one refunded game, for minus $362 at $100 a play (ROI minus 36.9%). We checked the sum from the listed results. Free picks are not the paid picks, and ten picks prove nothing either way. CapperTek says ASAWins.com "does not have a documented record yet", and VerifiedCappers shows no reviews.

What the store itself publishes: the SportsCapping streak table and a list of yearly leaderboard finishes such as #2 in the NFL in 2023 at 63-35. We recomputed every win rate and they match. The profits are small next to the volume: the 148-126 NBA run is $879 at $100 a play, about +8.8 units over 274 plays or roughly 3% return, and the 92-73 football run is about +11.1 units over 165 plays. On 19 Nov 2026 Vegas Experts showed the previous day's four ASA plays at 2-2, which by our count is minus $18 at the listed prices.
SportsCapping sells the picks, grades them and publishes the tables, so the store and the scorekeeper are the same company.

our_data.text: In this edition no ASA pick is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how ASA performs.

customers_intro: We found very little written by buyers. The posts we could open are TheRX forum threads from December 2005 and January 2006, plus 2026 forum rules that list ASA. Review widgets on the affiliate sites had no ratings, and our Reddit archive search found nothing.

customers.text: We found about six relevant forum posts, all on TheRX, almost all from three threads in late December 2005 and early January 2006 when members were hunting for ASA's 7 star Bowl Game of the Year. Two members who said they lived in Madison or had dealt with the owners described them as honest, friendly and easy to reach, and one said ASA had not lost a 7 star or bigger play that season. Others were sceptical: one member said people keep paying good money for losers, and another joked that the big play was the team losing. We found no recent buyer reviews on Reddit, Covers, Sportsbook Review, BBB, CapperTek, VerifiedCappers or the affiliate review widgets. In 2026 TheRX lists ASA among services whose plays members may not post.

A TheRX member wrote that of all the bad things people say about services, ASA is not one of them. The member called it "an honest service" that you can stop in and talk with, said they had talked games with them many times and found them down to earth, and credited the owners with Doc's Big Ten Game of the Year streak before they left.
In the same thread another member said the owners were real, solid people based in Madison and guessed which bowl team their big play would be on.

A member corrected another poster who thought ASA had lost its big play, saying ASA had not lost a 7 star or higher play all season and that the Bowl Game of the Year had not been released yet. A Madison member added that ASA had been 7 star on Baltimore in the NFL that week. We did not verify these claims.

When members identified ASA's 7 star Bowl Game of the Year as Auburn, one long time member joked that it was the team losing by 24 points, and another said they had just finished a 13-1 run for free while people were still paying good money for losers.
TheRX's daily service play threads list ASA among the services members may not post, and separately list "ASA, ASA Inc’s or American Sports Analysts" among services whose write ups may not be posted.

We found no BBB profile for American Sports Analysts, no app store listing and no testimonials on ASAwins.com. VerifiedCappers shows 0 reviews, Capper Reviews shows "No votes yet", and CapperTek shows no documented record. Our Reddit archive search for asawins in r/sportsbook returned no posts; full text comment searches timed out.

conflicts: Vegas Experts, Boyd's Bets, Capper Reviews and Professional Sports Picks all show the same ASA packages with checkout links to SportsCapping. Capper Reviews states that it is part of the SportsCapping network, which sells ASA's picks. Review pages on these sites come from the seller's own sales channel.
SportsCapping grades ASA's picks, ranks them on its own leaderboards and sells them, so the store is also the scorekeeper.
ASAwins.com resells other pick brands (Nelly's, Point Train, Cover Kings, J's Plays) alongside its own picks.
strengths: A long and traceable history: the founders' names, a Wisconsin corporation in the site terms and a public PPP loan record for American Sports Analysts Inc in Madison.
Written analysis with each play, not just a team name; the graded plays we saw each came with a full paragraph of reasoning.
The store shows losing results too, including the previous day's losses and an 8-11 figure for the 3 day pass this season.
Low cost ways to try it: a $19.95 daily basketball package on ASAwins.com and free picks posted several times a week.
Forum members who said they knew the owners in 2005 described them as honest and easy to reach.
concerns: Every published record is a streak with its own start date; no full pick history from a fixed date is shown.
Profit figures for the same sport differ across pages ($55,590, $46,170 and $38,360 for basketball; $19,820 and $27,980 for hockey).
The "pay only when you win" promise on ASAwins.com has no written terms we could find, and the site terms disclaim all warranties.
On the SportsCapping network a losing term only earns a free term, never cash, and season passes have no guarantee at all.
The only outside log we found, of ASA's free picks, was 3-6 for minus 36.9% over the last 30 days: a tiny sample, but not a good one.
History claims conflict (since 1987, 1989 or 1997; 40+, 50+ or 55+ years), and the same package costs different amounts on different sites.
checklist: Ask ASA in writing what "pay only when you win" means before you buy on ASAwins.com, and keep the answer.
Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, odds and time it was sent. A run that starts on a chosen date is not a record.
Count units, not wins: 54% at -110 is only a few units over hundreds of plays.
Compare the price on ASAwins.com, SportsCapping and Big Al before buying; the same picks can cost more or less.
Remember that season passes on SportsCapping carry no guarantee, and no option refunds cash.
Write each pick down the moment it arrives, with the line you can actually get.
faq: It is a real business: American Sports Analysts, Inc, run by Lee Kostroski and Mike Merlet since 1997 according to its own pages, with a Wisconsin address and a public PPP loan record. Whether its picks win over time is not shown; its records are streaks graded by its own sales network.

On 19 Nov 2026 ASAwins.com listed $19.95 for a daily basketball package, $85 for 7 days, $295 for November football, $395 to $495 for football seasons, $695 for the NBA season and $995 for the basketball combo. SportsCapping sites charged $35 a pick, $124.99 for 3 days, $174.99 for 7 days and $394.99 for 30 days.
Does ASA have a verified record?

No. SportsCapping shows streaks such as 148-126 in top NBA plays since 30 Oct 2025 and 50-33 in top college football plays since 29 Nov 2025, graded by itself. CapperTek has no documented record, and a third party log of ASA's free picks showed 3-6 over the last 30 days.
What does "pay only when you win" mean at ASA?

We could not find written terms on ASAwins.com. On the SportsCapping network, the written policy gives one free term of equal length after a losing paid term, no cash refunds, and nothing on season passes.

Its pages name Lee Kostroski and Mike Merlet, who say they started at Doc's Enterprises before founding ASA Inc in 1997. The site terms give American Sports Analysts, Inc, PO Box 930526, Verona, WI 53593.

It is a long running service that writes up its plays and shows some losses. But nothing we could open proves it beats the 52.4% needed at -110 over a fixed, full period, and its own NBA run is only about a 3% return. Try the cheapest option first and track it yourself.
